short.q: 12 g of Mg burns in 4 g of O₂: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. Identify the limiting reactant and the mass of MgO formed. (Mg 24, O 16) [4]
short.model: O₂ is limiting: 4 g = 0.125 mol needs 0.25 mol Mg, but 0.5 mol Mg is present. MgO formed = 0.25 mol × 40 = 10 g.
points: O₂ needs only 0.25 mol Mg so O₂ limiting

short.q: CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂. Calculate the volume of CO₂ at r.t.p. from 5 g CaCO₃ in excess acid. (Ca 40, C 12, O 16) [3]
short.model: 5 g = 0.05 mol; 1:1 ratio so 0.05 mol CO₂; volume = 0.05 × 24 = 1.2 dm³ (1200 cm³).

short.q: Describe a test for water and give the result. [2]
short.model: Add the liquid to anhydrous copper(II) sulfate, which turns from white to blue (or anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride, blue to pink).
points: anhydrous copper(II) sulfate or cobalt(II) chloride
white to blue / blue to pink

short.q: Calculate the mass of copper(II) oxide formed when 6.4 g of copper reacts completely with oxygen: 2Cu + O₂ → 2CuO. (Cu 64, O 16) [3]
short.model: 6.4 g Cu = 0.1 mol; 0.1 mol CuO; Mr = 80; mass = 8 g.

short.q: Explain why an excess of metal is used when preparing a salt from a metal and an acid. [2]
short.model: Excess metal ensures all the acid reacts; the unreacted metal is then removed by filtration.
points: excess is solid so filtered off
